options.content: **Queue → execute → commit → publish.** Worker selection filters DB and worker charts; scrape, overall coverage and RSS stay instance-wide. **No data ≠ healthy.** Hover a panel’s ⓘ for measurement details.

panels.title: Scrape up
panels.description: Exporter scrape status; does not prove worker or DB coverage.

panels.title: Worker coverage
panels.description: Covered / expected workers for the entire instance.

panels.title: DB telemetry / covered
panels.description: Selected workers with ordered SQLite telemetry / covered selected workers. Missing worker coverage is shown separately.

panels.title: Process RSS
panels.description: One process-wide RSS sample, replicated on worker series. Maximum avoids multiplying process memory by worker count. Includes SQLite and all other process memory.

panels.title: Reader jobs completed / s
panels.description: Completed jobs on the reader lane, including non-OK results. Counts jobs, not SQL statements, rows or physical IOPS. Streamed chunks are not additional jobs.

panels.title: Writer jobs completed / s
panels.description: Completed jobs on the writer lane, including background maintenance, polling, jobs with no data changes and non-OK results. Not changed rows, SQLite page writes, fsyncs or physical IOPS. See SQLite page activity for pager counters.

panels.title: Writer publication p99
panels.description: Admission to first completion publication, including queueing and commit. No traffic means no percentile.

panels.title: DB errors / s
panels.description: Non-OK results; BUSY is a subset. Does not include later streaming-delivery failures.

panels.title: DB jobs by executor lane
panels.description: Jobs admitted to each lane and their first completion publications, including non-OK results. Writer jobs include background maintenance and polling even when no data changes. These are not SQL statements, changed rows, page writes, fsyncs or physical IOPS. See SQLite page activity for pager counters. Gaps are not filled with zero.

panels.title: Publication latency / p95 · p99
panels.description: End-to-end DB publication latency. Percentiles are computed from merged histogram buckets, never averaged across workers.

panels.title: Admission refusals & errors
panels.description: Connection and worker refusals are retryable overload. Unavailable is not. Errors count failed jobs after admission; BUSY is a subset of errors.

panels.title: Request credit utilization
panels.description: In-flight includes completed output until release: this is admission pressure, not queue length. The axis scales to observed load; 100% is the admission limit.

panels.title: Byte credit utilization
panels.description: Charged request/output credits, not SQLite heap or process memory.

panels.title: Writer request allowance
panels.description: Writer capacity is total capacity minus reserved reader requests. Per-connection fairness may reject earlier.

panels.title: Writer byte allowance
panels.description: Writer budget excludes reserved reader bytes. Readers may use otherwise idle write capacity.

panels.title: Writer stages / p95
panels.description: Queue includes FIFO dependencies, lazy open and group collection. Execution excludes commit. Publication includes all earlier stages and cleanup. These percentiles overlap and must not be added.

panels.title: Reader stages / p95
panels.description: Queue includes FIFO dependencies, lazy open and group collection. Execution excludes commit. Publication includes all earlier stages and cleanup. These percentiles overlap and must not be added.

panels.title: Commit & projection finalization / p95 · p99
panels.description: One observation per writer transaction, including failures. COMMIT may include synchronous auto-checkpoint work; this is not an isolated fsync timer.

panels.title: Publication p99 / worker
panels.description: Locate a slow submitting worker. Shared executors attribute work to the submitting worker; these are not executor thread IDs.

panels.title: Mean group size
panels.description: Attempted grouped jobs / attempted group transactions, including failed groups. Not fsync savings. No groups gives no value.

panels.title: Pager hit ratio / worker
panels.description: SQLite pager hits / (hits + misses). Not OS cache hit ratio. Idle workers have no ratio.

panels.title: SQLite page activity
panels.description: SQLite pager counters, separate from executor job counts. Page writes count pages written from SQLite's cache, not physical IOPS, disk bytes or fsyncs. Cache misses are not necessarily physical disk reads. Includes lazy connection initialization.

panels.title: Connections / worker
panels.description: Live connections on selected workers, including monitoring connections.

panels.title: Transient send-buffer budget
panels.description: Live pooled send-buffer bytes relative to a reporting budget. Not total worker heap usage and not an allocation cap; can exceed 100%.

panels.title: I/O completion rate
panels.description: Worker io_uring completions; SQLite executor work is separate.

panels.title: I/O mean measured latency
panels.description: Latency sum / sample count rates. No denominator clamp: rates below one sample/s remain correct. No samples gives no value.

panels.title: I/O ring occupancy
panels.description: (Ring depth - available entries) / ring depth. This is not total pending I/O.

panels.title: Pending & unqueued I/O
panels.description: Pending operations and current unqueued depth. The legacy sq_overflow name is a gauge, not a cumulative overflow counter.

panels.title: Worker coverage & DB availability
panels.description: A covered worker can lack SQLite telemetry. Missing DB samples remain absent; never synthesize zero-valued counters.

panels.title: Last received stats age
panels.description: Exporter-local receive age. Excludes zero timestamps for never-observed/disconnected workers; inspect coverage alongside this chart.

panels.title: Bot send-queue utilization
panels.description: Only monitoring bot connections, not every client on a worker. Backpressure is a boolean marker, not utilization.

panels.title: Stats requests & responses
panels.description: Legacy ping/pong metric names track collector statistics polling. Difference in short windows is not proof of a lost response.

panels.title: Collector errors
panels.description: Connection, read, decode, protocol and polling errors. These are not SQLite job errors.

panels.title: Instance coverage diagnostics
panels.description: Instance-wide counts, independent of the worker selector. A count mismatch compares observed and configured worker counts.

options.content:
**DB jobs ≠ disk writes.** Reader/writer rates count executor jobs. Background maintenance, polling, jobs with no data changes and failed jobs all count. SQLite page activity is separate; page writes are not physical IOPS or fsyncs.

**Unavailable telemetry ≠ zero load.** Histograms need observations; idle periods can have no percentile. Scrape health, worker coverage and SQLite availability are separate signals.

**Not instrumented here:** SQLite WAL bytes, separate checkpoint backlog/duration, isolated fsync time, query-level timings, client retry exhaustion and retained-chat storage. Legacy entity-WAL and compaction panels were removed because their compatibility fields are always zero.

**Memory:** process RSS is shown once; buffer utilization covers transient sends only. **Latency:** DB publication stops before full streamed delivery and WebSocket ACK. Cache counters count pages, not disk bytes.

title: NRC Metrics Service
description: SQLite executor health, admission pressure, latency, worker transport and collector coverage. One NRC instance per view.
